text:
Nazem Kadri is 36, in his second stint in Colorado, and still getting to the front of the net like a much younger man. Five goals on nine expected goals is the story of his season: he is getting 1.38 expected goals per 60 minutes, up from 0.91 last season, and they just aren't going in. He hasn't scored in five games despite 3.5 expected goals in that stretch, including a 1.44 night in Montreal on Nov. 14.

That's the kind of drought we'd call due. Shooting 8.3% against a league average of 13.4% isn't who he's been over 1,000-plus NHL games and 323 career goals before this season.

The assists have kept him relevant, 17 points in 21 games with eight on the power play. A new line with Gabriel Landeskog and Nicolas Roy drew attention in Toronto from The Denver Post and Sportsnet, and the Avs have won six of their last ten. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 85th percentile for chances from the home-plate area last season. The looks are there. Watch for the finish to catch up.
